rules.intake: the approved S49 shared-launch brief plus the approved Skill-80 page request (offer, disclosure, route graph), consumed with per-field provenance; no separate questionnaire
rules.review_labels: the private client-review document labels each email with its framework and labels the body 'Email Body:'; the recipient payload carries no framework labels, slot instructions, or production commentary

variant_pairing.pairing: subject and preview are paired per variant (Pair A = subject A + preview A; Pair B = subject B + preview B); pairs are preserved through the Skill-44 draft handoff, never flattened into unpaired lists
variant_pairing.pair_b_style: pattern-breaking, truthful and on brand (no false account alert, no fake reply prefix, no fabricated urgency, no offensive language, no misleading price)

upsell_1.entry_context: verified original purchase; buyer reached Upsell 1 and left without accepting

upsell_2.entry_context: verified accepted Upsell 1 or verified accepted Downsell 1; buyer reached Upsell 2 and left without accepting
upsell_2.note: Upsell 2 is the final offer in the route graph; both accept and explicit decline finish at the thank-you / access handoff.

eligibility_rules.requires: verified succeeded original purchase before any upsell follow-up
eligibility_rules.upsell_2_qualifying_purchase: verified succeeded upsell_1 OR verified succeeded downsell_1
eligibility_rules.already_owned_action: suppress the offer email or route to the next page in the route graph

truth_rules: Honor the previous purchase in the opening of every email; the upgrade continues a good decision and never corrects it.
No invented deadline, countdown, seat cap, bonus expiry or price. Use scarcity ONLY when the page request carries factual_scarcity_evidence; empty evidence means zero scarcity language.
State the amount, currency and billing terms exactly as the page disclosure states them, including recurring terms when billing_type is recurring.
One destination per pattern: the matching upsell page. Never introduce an alternate offer.
Every CTA is the same guarded one-click action on the upsell page; when one-click is unavailable the page blocks the paid action and offers safe continuation — the email must not promise otherwise.
The next offer comes from the route graph, never from assumption.
rules.trigger: appended after each Skill-80 upsell page (upsell_1 or upsell_2) is written; one three-email sequence per page pattern
